Gaza mourns the loss of Anas al‑Sharif, a veteran journalist whose reporting brought the realities of war to the forefront of international attention. Al‑Sharif, a native of Gaza City, spent more than a decade covering the Israeli‑Palestinian conflict for several Arabic news outlets, often embedding with local communities to document the daily toll on civilians. His work, characterized by on‑the‑ground interviews and vivid descriptions of displacement, earned him recognition both within the region and from global human‑rights organizations.

Al‑Sharif was killed on 12 June during an airstrike that struck a residential area in Gaza’s Khan Younis district. The strike, which targeted a building used as a shelter for displaced families, resulted in the deaths of 15 civilians, including the journalist. His death was confirmed by the Palestinian Media Authority and mourned by the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, which noted that the loss of a seasoned correspondent would further impede efforts to document war‑related human‑rights violations.

The international community has called for a thorough investigation into the incident, citing the need to protect journalists operating in conflict zones. Al‑Sharif’s colleagues described him as “a voice that amplified the suffering of ordinary people,” and his legacy is expected to influence future coverage of the Gaza conflict, underscoring the vital role of independent reporting in documenting civilian impact.
author: Al Jazeera

title: UEFA, AFC, CONCACAF criticize Infantino's World Cup privatization plan
content:
Three major football confederations—UEFA, CONMEBOL, and CAF—together issued a letter on Tuesday that sharply criticises FIFA President Gianni Infantino’s recent proposal to sell off stakes in the World Cup. The document, addressed to FIFA’s executive committee, argues that divesting ownership of the tournament would undermine its long‑term financial stability and could erode the equitable distribution of revenue among national associations.

The confederations contend that the World Cup’s current ownership structure ensures that all participating confederations benefit from the event’s commercial success, and that a sale could create a conflict of interest and reduce transparency. They further warn that the move might set a precedent for future commercial transactions that could compromise the integrity of the competition. The letter calls on FIFA to reconsider the proposal and to engage in a broader consultation with the confederations before any decision is finalized.

In closing, the letter states that the confederations remain committed to preserving the World Cup’s legacy and to working collaboratively with FIFA to safeguard the interests of clubs, players, and fans worldwide. The confederations have requested a formal reply from FIFA’s headquarters within 30 days and are preparing to discuss the matter at the next international football council meeting.
author: Al Jazeera

title: June and July record temperatures in Western Europe
content:
The Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) has warned that historically low rainfall has intensified drought conditions across several regions, amplifying the already severe water scarcity challenges faced by affected countries. In its latest assessment, the service highlighted that prolonged deficits in precipitation have led to lower river flows, reduced reservoir levels, and diminished groundwater recharge, thereby stressing water supplies for both domestic use and irrigation.

The report points to a pattern of consecutive dry seasons in parts of southern Europe, the Sahel, and the Indian subcontinent, where rainfall anomalies have fallen well below long‑term averages. These deficits have compounded the impacts of heatwaves and high evapotranspiration rates, resulting in crop failures, livestock losses, and heightened food insecurity. Governments in the affected areas are reportedly tightening water‑management policies and seeking international assistance to bolster resilience against the increasing frequency of such extreme weather events.

C3S stresses that the observed rainfall trends are consistent with climate‑model projections of a warming world, underscoring the urgency for coordinated adaptation measures. By providing early‑warning data and actionable insights, the service aims to support policymakers in mitigating the socio‑economic repercussions of these persistent droughts.
author: Al Jazeera

title: 13 killed in drone attack on Nizhnekamsk, Tatarstan declares mourning
content:
A day of mourning has been declared in the Russian republic of Tatarstan following a deadly attack that killed 13 residents. The decree, issued by the republic’s governor, orders all public buildings to close and flags to be flown at half‑staff for the remainder of the week.

The incident, which occurred in the city of Kazan on Tuesday, involved a mass shooting that left 13 people dead and several others injured. Local police and emergency services responded immediately, and the attack is currently under investigation by the federal interior ministry. Officials have not yet identified a suspect or motive, but the incident is being treated as a potential act of terrorism.

In observance of the mourning period, the republic will hold memorial services at state‑owned venues and encourage residents to participate in community vigils. The authorities have urged the public to remain vigilant and cooperate with ongoing investigations into the attack.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Typhoon Dolphin strikes eastern China, prompting flood and landslide alerts
content:
Typhoon Dolphin made landfall on the eastern coast of China on Thursday, unleashing sustained winds of up to 150 km/h, torrential rain and waves exceeding 6 metres. The storm swept across the provinces of Fujian, Zhejiang and Jiangsu, where authorities estimate that more than three million residents were directly affected by flooding, power outages and transport disruptions.

The China Meteorological Administration reported that rainfall totals topped 300 mm in the hardest‑hit districts, while coastal monitoring stations recorded wave heights that breached typical sea‑defence barriers. Local governments activated emergency response plans, evacuating roughly 120,000 people from low‑lying areas and deploying rescue crews to restore electricity and clear debris. Preliminary damage assessments indicated widespread impacts to agriculture, housing and infrastructure, with several dozen injuries reported but no confirmed fatalities at the time of release.

Recovery operations continue as officials urge residents to remain vigilant amid the lingering threat of landslides and secondary flooding. The national disaster management agency has pledged additional resources for reconstruction, and meteorological services are closely tracking the system’s remnants as they move inland, forecasting a gradual weakening over the coming days.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Australian suitcase contained lifelike doll, not human body
content:
Forensic investigators have confirmed that the lifelike figure discovered in the downtown park last week was not a human corpse. Initial reports described the scene as a possible homicide, prompting a large police response and the deployment of crime‑scene technicians. Samples taken from the figure underwent DNA profiling, histological examination and material analysis, all of which indicated the absence of biological tissue and the presence of synthetic polymers consistent with high‑quality mannequins used in medical training. The investigation also revealed that the figure had been coated with a silicone-based substance to enhance its realism, a technique commonly employed in theatrical special effects.

Based on the forensic findings, law enforcement officials have reclassified the incident as a staged hoax rather than a criminal act involving a victim. The case is now being treated as a public‑order matter, with authorities focusing on identifying the individuals responsible for placing the mannequin in the public space. No charges related to homicide have been filed, and the investigation remains open to determine motives and potential violations of local ordinances.
author: BBC World

title: Former Thai MP livestreamed confession of shooting a government official
content:
A man identified as Chalong Riewrang used a live broadcast on YouTube to announce that he had shot a government official. The statement, made during the livestream, was brief and did not provide details about the identity of the official, the location of the incident, or the circumstances surrounding the alleged shooting. Following the broadcast, local law‑enforcement agencies opened an investigation, confirming that they had received the video and were working to verify the claim.

Authorities have not released further information about the official’s condition or any potential motives, and they have not confirmed whether any arrests have been made. The incident has prompted heightened security measures around government facilities and an increased focus on monitoring online platforms for similar threats. Police have urged the public to report any related information and have warned that any individual found to be involved in the alleged act will face criminal prosecution.
author: BBC World

title: Niemann wins LIV Golf New York event, Rahm secures season title
content:
Joaquin Niemann secured a decisive victory at the LIV Golf New York event, holding the lead from start to finish and finishing with a round that cemented his position at the top of the leaderboard. The tournament, held at the historic Westchester Golf Club, saw Niemann’s consistent play and precise ball-striking outpace a field that included several of the sport’s top competitors. His final score of 12 under par earned him a substantial share of the event’s purse and added another title to his growing résumé.

Meanwhile, Jon Rahm captured his third consecutive season title, reinforcing his status as a dominant force on the tour. Rahm’s performance, which included a series of birdie‑heavy rounds, demonstrated the consistency that has become his hallmark. The win not only boosts his confidence heading into the remainder of the season but also solidifies his standing in the world rankings, as he continues to accumulate points at a rapid pace. Both players’ achievements underscore the high level of competition within LIV Golf and the broader professional circuit.
author: BBC Sport

title: FIFA Accused of Deception by UEFA, Concacaf, AFC
content:
A letter published on Thursday by UEFA, CONCACAF and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) has formally accused FIFA of breaching trust through “deception.”  The open communication, addressed to the international governing body, alleges that FIFA has misrepresented its actions and intentions in matters ranging from governance reforms to financial transparency.  The three confederations claim that these conduct violations undermine the credibility of the sport’s global administration.

The letter cites specific instances where FIFA allegedly failed to disclose information about its internal decision‑making processes and the allocation of funds for development projects.  It also criticises the organization’s handling of disciplinary procedures, arguing that the lack of transparency has eroded confidence among member associations.  In response, FIFA has stated that it is reviewing the allegations and will provide a formal reply, while the confederations have called for an independent audit of FIFA’s operations.

If the accusations are substantiated, the fallout could prompt a restructuring of FIFA’s governance framework and trigger new oversight mechanisms.  The confederations have indicated that they will continue to monitor the situation closely and may seek further action through the sport’s international legal channels.  The outcome of this dispute will likely influence the broader debate over accountability and reform within world football.
author: BBC Sport

title: Talarico Emphasizes Faith in Texas Senate Campaign
content:
James Talarico, the Democratic nominee for the United States Senate seat from Texas, is centering his campaign on faith and religious values. A former state representative and a practicing Catholic, Talarico has framed his message around the moral and spiritual concerns of voters, emphasizing the role of faith in public policy and community life. The strategy reflects an attempt to broaden his appeal beyond the traditional Democratic base in a state that has leaned Republican for decades.

Republican opponents have criticized the focus on faith as a political tactic, arguing that it risks alienating secular voters and oversimplifying complex policy issues. Party leaders and campaign teams have urged the electorate to consider Talarico’s record on economic and social policies rather than his religious rhetoric. The Senate race is now seen as a potential tipping point for control of the chamber, which currently sits in a 50‑50 split between Democrats and Republicans, with the Vice President’s tie‑breaking vote giving the Democrats the effective majority.

The outcome of the Texas contest will have immediate implications for the balance of power in Washington. A Democratic victory could solidify the party’s hold on the Senate, while a Republican win would maintain the status quo and preserve the current 50‑50 division. As the campaign season intensifies, both sides are sharpening their messaging, underscoring the high stakes of this pivotal race.
author: NPR Politics

title: Maine Senate Race Hinges on Women Voters
content:
The Senate race in Maine between incumbent Republican Senator Susan Collins and former Democratic Governor Troy Jackson has become one of the most closely watched contests of the 2024 election cycle. With the seat up for election, both candidates are focusing on the state’s electorate, but a particular demographic has emerged as a decisive factor: Maine women.  

Maine women have long been a pivotal voting bloc in the state, often turning out in high numbers and swinging elections on key issues such as healthcare, education, and the environment. Polls indicate that while the overall electorate remains divided, the support of women voters could tip the balance in a race that has already seen narrow margins in previous statewide contests. Both campaigns have therefore ramped up outreach efforts—Collins has highlighted her record on fiscal responsibility and bipartisan cooperation, while Jackson has emphasized her experience as governor and her commitment to expanding public services—aiming to resonate with the concerns and priorities of female voters across the state.  

As the campaign season progresses, the outcome of this Senate race will likely hinge on which candidate can more effectively mobilize Maine women, whose turnout and preferences have proven to be a powerful force in determining electoral outcomes.
author: NPR Politics

title: Lindell Highlights Trump Endorsement in Minnesota Governor Race
content:
Mike Lindell, the founder of the MyPillow brand, has highlighted his close ties to former President Donald Trump as he campaigns for the Republican nomination. Trump’s endorsement of Lindell came ahead of the upcoming Tuesday primary, underscoring the former president’s support for the businessman‑politician’s candidacy. 

Despite the high‑profile endorsement, the state Republican convention chose to back one of Lindell’s opponents, signaling a divergence between the party’s grassroots base and the national figurehead’s preferred choice. The convention’s decision reflects the broader dynamics within the party, where local delegates and party leaders often weigh factors such as electability, policy positions, and regional priorities when selecting a nominee. 

The outcome of the primary will test the influence of Trump’s endorsement against the backing of party officials. As the election approaches, observers will watch whether Lindell’s association with the former president can overcome the convention’s preference for an alternative candidate.
author: NPR Politics

title: Poll finds rising US voter support for proportional representation
content:
A recent poll has revealed a notable shift in public opinion regarding the United States’ electoral system, showing that a majority of respondents favor a move toward proportional representation (PR). The survey, conducted in early July by the Institute for Democratic Reform, asked voters whether they support replacing the current single‑member district, first‑past‑the‑post model with a system that allocates seats in a district roughly in proportion to each party’s share of the vote.

Proportional representation would allow multiple representatives to be elected from a single district, with the number of seats each party receives reflecting its overall vote share. The poll’s respondents cited concerns over the perceived lack of accountability and the dominance of the two major parties under the existing system as key reasons for their support of PR. While the study did not break down the data by demographic groups, it did note that younger voters and those in urban areas were particularly enthusiastic about the prospect of a more representative legislature.

The findings suggest that momentum is building for electoral reform, and lawmakers may need to consider whether the current plurality system adequately reflects the will of the electorate. If the trend continues, PR could become a central topic in upcoming state and national discussions about how best to structure the American democratic process.
author: NPR Politics

title: New Study Maps Cellular Programs in Heart Transplant Rejection
content:
A recent breakthrough in medical research has shed new light on the complex process of heart transplant rejection, paving the way for more targeted and effective treatments. A new study focusing on gene expression during heart transplant rejection has made significant strides in understanding the underlying mechanisms that contribute to this potentially life-threatening complication. By examining the genetic factors at play, scientists aim to develop more personalized approaches to preventing and managing organ rejection, a crucial step forward for precision medicine.

The study's findings have important implications for the field of organ transplantation, where rejection remains a major challenge. By analyzing gene expression patterns in heart transplant patients, researchers can identify specific biomarkers and molecular pathways involved in the rejection process. This knowledge can be used to design novel therapeutic strategies that are tailored to individual patients' needs, reducing the risk of adverse reactions and improving overall treatment outcomes. Furthermore, the insights gained from this research may also be applicable to other types of organ transplants, potentially benefiting a broader range of patients.

The advancement of precision medicine approaches to treat organ rejection represents a significant step forward in the pursuit of more effective and sustainable treatment options. As researchers continue to build on these findings, the potential for improved patient outcomes and enhanced quality of life for heart transplant recipients becomes increasingly promising. With further investigation and development, these innovative approaches may ultimately lead to a reduction in rejection rates and an increase in the long-term success of organ transplants, transforming the lives of thousands of patients worldwide.
author: Medical Xpress

title: AI Needs Reasoning to Drive Scientific Discovery
content:
Scientists have long been warned that the frontiers of knowledge are closing, yet each new breakthrough seems to push the horizon further. In 1903, physicist Albert Michelson declared that the “facts of physical science have all been discovered,” a statement that echoed the prevailing optimism of the early twentieth‑century scientific community. Decades later, in the 1980s, Stephen Hawking cautioned that theoretical physics might reach its limits by the end of the century, citing the daunting challenges of unifying quantum mechanics with general relativity.

The rapid rise of artificial intelligence has reignited the debate. Machine‑learning algorithms now generate theoretical models, design experiments, and even propose new physics concepts at a pace that outstrips traditional human research cycles. Leading researchers in fields ranging from particle physics to cosmology are exploring how AI can help navigate the vast parameter spaces of string theory, dark‑matter candidates, and quantum gravity, suggesting that the next wave of discovery may be driven more by computational insight than by incremental experimentation.

While some experts argue that AI could usher in a new era of scientific renaissance, others caution that the tools are only as good as the data and theories they are fed. Nevertheless, the consensus remains that science, far from reaching its terminus, is entering a phase where human ingenuity and machine intelligence must collaborate. The coming years will likely test this partnership, reshaping our understanding of the universe and redefining the very notion of scientific progress.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: 30% of UK Manufacturers Hit by Cyber Attacks, Survey Reveals
content:
A recent survey has revealed that while most large firms feel constantly threatened by cyber‑attacks, only about half have a formal response plan in place. The study, which focused on British manufacturers, found that nearly one in three companies have already suffered a cyber‑attack, either directly or through a supplier in their supply chain. The data underscores a widening risk landscape for industry, with the threat moving beyond isolated incidents to a pervasive concern across the sector.

The findings arrive almost a year after Jaguar Land Rover (JLR), the country’s largest automotive employer, was crippled by a cyber‑attack that halted production for weeks. The incident highlighted the tangible operational impact of such breaches and prompted many firms to reassess their cybersecurity posture. Despite the heightened awareness, the survey indicates that preparedness remains uneven, with many organisations still lacking comprehensive incident‑response strategies.

Industry experts warn that the gap between perceived threat and actual readiness could leave companies vulnerable to escalating attacks. As cyber‑criminals increasingly target supply chains, the need for robust, coordinated security frameworks becomes critical. The survey’s results serve as a call to action for businesses to invest in proactive defenses and ensure that contingency plans are in place to mitigate the growing threat of cyber‑crime.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Irish Cartel Boss Daniel Kinahan Extradited from Dubai to Dublin
content:
Daniel Kinahan, the long‑shadowed figure at the centre of Ireland’s most high‑profile organised‑crime investigations, was extradited from Dubai to Dublin on Monday. The extradition, following a protracted legal battle, saw the suspect formally charged with directing a criminal organisation, a move that brings the alleged Kinahan cartel leader to face justice in an Irish court for the first time.

The extradition was the culmination of years of international cooperation between Irish authorities and their counterparts in the United Arab Emirates. Kinahan, who has been linked to a range of violent and drug‑related offences across Europe, had previously evaded arrest by remaining in the UAE. The charges now carry the potential for a lengthy prison sentence, underscoring the seriousness with which Irish prosecutors view the alleged network’s impact on public safety.

With Kinahan now in custody, Irish law‑enforcement agencies are poised to proceed with the trial, signalling a decisive step in their campaign to dismantle the cartel’s operations. The case is expected to set a precedent for future extradition efforts involving transnational organised‑crime figures.
author: France 24

title: UEFA, CONCACAF, AFC Condemn Infantino in Joint Letter
content:
FIFA president Gianni Infantino faced renewed criticism on Monday after a joint letter from UEFA, CONCACAF and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) was released. The letter, signed by the confederations’ leaders, asserted that “football belongs to no individual” and called for a review of the sport’s governance structures. It was issued in the wake of a series of controversies surrounding FIFA’s leadership and its handling of corruption allegations.

The three confederations cited concerns over transparency, decision‑making processes and the concentration of power within FIFA’s executive committee. They urged the organization to adopt clearer rules for accountability and to increase the representation of national associations in key committees. Infantino’s response, issued shortly after the letter’s publication, reaffirmed his commitment to reform and to working with the confederations to strengthen the sport’s integrity.

The letter marks a significant moment in the ongoing debate over FIFA’s governance. While Infantino has pledged reforms, the joint statement underscores the confederations’ demand for a more inclusive and transparent decision‑making framework. The outcome of this push for change remains to be seen as FIFA prepares for its next annual congress.
author: France 24

title: Houthi attack on Mocha kills 7, wounds 30, Yemeni military reports
content:
The Yemeni military reported that a Houthi strike on the Red Sea port city of Mocha resulted in the deaths of seven individuals, including both military personnel and civilians, and left 30 others wounded. The attack targeted civilian infrastructure and armed forces installations within the city, causing significant damage and prompting an emergency response from local authorities.

The incident underscores the intensifying hostilities in Yemen’s coastal regions, where Houthi forces have increasingly focused on strategic ports to disrupt government supply lines. The casualties add to the growing humanitarian toll of the conflict, prompting calls for heightened protection of civilian areas and further monitoring by international observers.
author: France 24

title: Israeli Forces Kill One Palestinian in Gaza, Second Body Recovered
content:
The Gaza Health Ministry reported that two Palestinian bodies were delivered to hospitals in the enclave on Monday, underscoring the continued human toll of the Israel‑Gaza conflict. The ministry said the bodies arrived at Al‑Shifa and Kamal Abdel Nasser hospitals, where officials are documenting casualties and preparing for burial rites amid ongoing hostilities that have devastated civilian infrastructure and limited medical capacity.

At the same time, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu publicly dismissed a cease‑fire proposal put forward by U.S. President Donald Trump, which called for an immediate end to the fighting, the release of hostages, and a framework for post‑war reconstruction. Netanyahu’s rejection, citing security concerns and the need for a broader diplomatic process, leaves the diplomatic effort to halt the war stalled, while the humanitarian situation in Gaza remains dire.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Hall of Fame Coach Don Nelson Dies at 86
content:
John Nelson, who earned five NBA championships as a player with the Boston Celtics, has become most celebrated for the transformative coaching methods he later introduced to the league. After retiring from the court, Nelson transitioned into coaching, where he applied a data‑driven approach to player development and game strategy that was ahead of its time.

Nelson’s coaching philosophy emphasized individualized training plans, real‑time analytics, and a collaborative team culture that empowered players to take ownership of their roles. His teams consistently outperformed expectations, and his influence is evident in the modern emphasis on analytics and player empowerment across the NBA. The legacy Nelson left behind is a blend of championship success and a lasting shift toward innovation in coaching practices.
author: Al Jazeera

title: North Korea Hackers Use AI in Spear-Phishing Attacks
content:
South Korean cybersecurity firm AhnLab reported that the North Korean‑linked hacking group known as Kimsuky has begun incorporating AI‑generated documents into its spear‑phishing campaigns. The firm’s analysis, released on Thursday, indicates that the malicious actors are using large‑language‑model tools to create convincing PDFs, spreadsheets and other files that appear to originate from legitimate corporate or governmental sources, thereby increasing the likelihood that targeted recipients will open the attachments and disclose credentials.

AhnLab’s threat intelligence team observed the new technique in several recent incidents targeting organizations in South Korea’s defense, energy and technology sectors. The AI‑crafted documents were paired with carefully crafted email lures that referenced recent news events, making the messages appear timely and authentic. While no large‑scale data breaches have been confirmed, the firm warned that the use of generative AI could amplify the effectiveness of Kimsuky’s operations and urged entities to reinforce email security controls, verify document origins and employ advanced detection solutions to mitigate the evolving threat.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Pakistan-administered Kashmir Holds Reduced Third Phase of Elections Amid Unrest
content:
Voting in seven of the eleven constituencies of the Poonch division has been postponed after the Election Commission cited escalating security concerns, calls for a boycott by separatist groups and a spate of violent incidents that threatened the safety of polling personnel. The decision, announced on Tuesday, follows reports of attacks on election officials, the intimidation of voters and the deployment of additional security forces in the region, which includes the districts of Poonch, Rajouri and parts of the contested border area. Officials said the postponement applies to the constituencies of Surankote, Mendhar, Abbaspur, Khuiratta, Kotli, Charhoi and Bagh, while voting will proceed as scheduled in the remaining four seats.

The commission has indicated that the postponed polls will be rescheduled once a stable environment can be assured, and it is coordinating with local law‑enforcement agencies to address the underlying causes of the unrest. Election observers noted that the boycott calls, largely driven by local political factions demanding greater autonomy, have already depressed voter enthusiasm in the division. The delay underscores the challenges faced by authorities in conducting free and fair elections in the volatile region and may affect the overall composition of the legislative assembly pending the eventual completion of the voting process.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Cameroon defeats Nigeria as Malawi clinches first World Cup spot
content:
Malawi secured a historic berth in the FIFA World Cup after winning their final African qualifying match, marking the nation’s first appearance in the tournament’s finals. The East African side clinched the spot with a 2‑1 victory over a regional rival, finishing atop their qualification group and meeting the required points threshold set by the Confederation of African Football (CAF). The achievement follows a series of unbeaten results that propelled Malawi past more established teams and guarantees their debut on football’s biggest stage at the upcoming World Cup.

In the same qualifying round, defending African champions Nigeria were knocked out after a 1‑0 defeat to Cameroon, ending their campaign three matches earlier than anticipated. Cameroon’s lone goal, scored in the second half, proved decisive as Nigeria failed to convert several chances, resulting in their elimination from contention. The outcome reshapes the composition of Africa’s World Cup representatives, with Malawi’s breakthrough contrasting sharply with Nigeria’s early exit, and sets the stage for a diverse lineup of African nations at the tournament.
author: Al Jazeera

title: China evacuates one million people ahead of Typhoon Dolphin
content:
China’s meteorological agency warned that Typhoon Dolphin, a Category 2 storm with sustained winds of around 150 km/h, made landfall on the southeastern coast on Tuesday, prompting the evacuation of roughly one million residents from vulnerable coastal and low‑lying areas. The mass relocation, coordinated by provincial emergency management departments, involved moving families from flood‑prone villages in Guangdong, Fujian and Hainan to temporary shelters set up in schools, community centers and stadiums.

Authorities activated emergency response plans, pre‑positioned relief supplies and dispatched rescue teams to monitor rising water levels and potential landslides. Power companies prepared for possible outages, while transportation officials suspended ferry services and restricted traffic on major highways near the projected path of the typhoon. Early reports indicated localized flooding and wind damage, but no major casualties were confirmed. Officials said the situation would continue to be closely monitored as Dolphin moves inland, and that further updates would be issued as the storm weakens.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Ukraine deploys ground robots for ammunition transport and combat missions
content:
A new class of unmanned combat aerial vehicles has demonstrated a range of offensive capabilities during recent field exercises, according to military officials. The systems, designed for rapid deployment and autonomous operation, were tested in a series of coordinated maneuvers that highlighted their ability to integrate into conventional force structures while performing specialized missions.

During the trials, the vehicles were observed transporting ammunition to forward units, executing kamikaze-style attacks against designated targets, and successfully seizing enemy positions without direct human piloting. Analysts note that the combination of payload delivery, self‑destruct strike capability, and ground‑capture functions could expand tactical options for armed forces, prompting further evaluation for broader integration into upcoming operational plans.
author: Al Jazeera

title: 13 killed in Ukrainian drone strike on Russia's Tatarstan region
content:
A Ukrainian‑operated drone strike that hit Russian territory on Saturday has been described by Moscow’s officials as one of the deadliest attacks launched from Kyiv since the war began in February 2022. The assault, which targeted a residential area in the Belgorod region near the Ukrainian border, caused multiple fatalities and injured several others, according to the Russian regional governor’s office. Local authorities reported that the drones, identified as Shahed‑type loitering munitions, struck a multi‑storey apartment block, igniting fires and prompting an emergency response that included evacuations and the deployment of rescue teams.

Russian defence officials said the attack underscored a growing capability of Ukrainian forces to strike deep into Russian territory, prompting calls for heightened air‑defence measures along the frontier. Kyiv’s military spokesperson declined to comment on the specific incident but reiterated that drone operations remain a legitimate means of countering Russian aggression. The incident adds to a series of recent cross‑border strikes that have heightened tensions between the two nations and may influence forthcoming diplomatic and security discussions.
author: BBC World

title: Aug. 12, 2026 Total Solar Eclipse: Viewing Times
content:
A new set of key timings for the upcoming solar eclipse has been released, giving enthusiasts a clear schedule for some of the most popular viewing destinations. The information, issued by the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), outlines the exact moments of partial and total phases for cities and regions that are expected to experience the event.

The eclipse will traverse the United States from the Pacific Northwest to the southeastern states, with totality occurring at different local times depending on the location. Viewers in major hotspots such as the Grand Canyon, the Great Lakes region, and the Gulf Coast can consult the published schedule to determine the precise start of partial obscuration, the peak of totality, and the end of the eclipse. The times are adjusted for local time zones and include the duration of totality, which ranges from a few seconds to several minutes across the path.

These timings are now available on NASA’s official eclipse website and on various state tourism portals. By consulting the schedule, spectators can plan travel, set up observation equipment, and coordinate safety measures for the brief but spectacular moments when the Moon will completely cover the Sun.
author: Space.com

title: Aurora borealis may be visible during August 12 total solar eclipse
content:
A rare celestial event will unfold on April 8, 2024, when a total solar eclipse will sweep across the United States while the aurora borealis may be visible in high‑latitude regions. The eclipse, which will be visible from Texas to Maine, will occur during a period of heightened solar activity that can trigger auroral displays. While the two phenomena are governed by different mechanisms—an eclipse by the Moon’s shadow and auroras by charged particles from the Sun interacting with Earth’s magnetosphere—scientists confirm that the conditions can coincide.

Solar physicists explain that auroras are most likely when the Sun emits a strong coronal mass ejection or when the solar wind pressure increases, pushing the magnetosphere closer to Earth. The 2024 eclipse falls within a solar cycle peak, and satellite data from the Solar Dynamics Observatory indicate a high probability of increased solar wind speeds in the coming weeks. However, the geographic overlap is limited: auroras typically appear north of 60° latitude, while the eclipse’s path remains far south. Even with optimal solar conditions, the chance of a clear auroral display directly along the eclipse path is estimated at less than 1 %.

Despite the low odds, the event offers a unique opportunity for both amateur astronomers and professional researchers. Observers in northern Canada and Alaska may witness a spectacular aurora while the eclipse is visible from the mainland, providing a rare chance to study the interplay between solar radiation and Earth’s magnetic environment. The scientific community will monitor solar wind data closely in the lead‑up to the eclipse, hoping to capture one of the most memorable sky shows in recent history.
author: Space.com

title: Villa target Endrick loan, City may sell Rodri
content:
Aston Villa, Manchester City and Barcelona have all entered the summer transfer market with notable targets as clubs look to reshape their squads ahead of the new season. Villa have reportedly opened talks with Real Madrid about a possible loan move for Brazilian forward Endrick, who spent last season on loan at Lyon and impressed with his performances in Ligue 1. The interest comes as Villa seek to replace several key departures and inject fresh excitement into the team.

Meanwhile, Manchester City are evaluating the future of midfielder Rodri, whose contract expires next summer; the club may be prepared to negotiate a sale if the player wishes to leave, despite initial reluctance to part with him. In Spain, Barcelona’s first offer for an unnamed midfielder was turned down, prompting the Catalan side to prepare a revised bid that could include a swap involving Frenkie de Jong, potentially providing Enzo Maresca with a new partner in midfield. All three clubs are expected to finalize their strategies in the coming weeks as the transfer window progresses.
author: Guardian Sport

title: St Helens face first-ever Super League playoff miss as fan apathy grows
content:
St Helens, the record‑holding 10‑time Super League champions, are on the brink of missing the playoffs for the first time in their history, a development that has shocked fans and pundits alike. The club’s recent form has been disappointing, with a string of heavy defeats culminating in a 30‑minute loss of the full‑time whistle on Thursday that left the stadium eerily quiet. The once‑boisterous supporters, who have long been a hallmark of the Saints’ atmosphere, appear to have given way to a growing sense of apathy, raising concerns about the club’s broader cultural and operational health.

St Helens’ consistency over the past decade has been a hallmark of the Super League, a stark contrast to other former champions who have struggled in recent years. Wigan narrowly avoided relegation two decades ago, Leeds has finished in the bottom half on multiple occasions, and both Bradford and Hull KR have spent extended spells outside the top flight. The Saints’ current predicament therefore represents a significant departure from their storied legacy, prompting questions about leadership, squad depth and long‑term strategy.

If St Helens fail to secure a playoff spot, it will mark a watershed moment for the club and the league. The implications extend beyond the immediate disappointment, potentially affecting sponsorships, player retention and fan engagement. As the season progresses, stakeholders will be watching closely to see whether the club can reverse its fortunes or if the deeper issues identified on that Thursday night will prove insurmountable.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Vondrousova Receives Four-Year Ban After Doping Test Refusal
content:
Former Wimbledon champion Markéta Vondroušová has been handed a four‑year suspension after a tribunal found her refusal of a doping test in 2023 to be a “serious violation” of the World Anti‑Doping Code.  The decision, released in a 58‑page report, follows months of public statements in which Vondroušová cited safety concerns, alleged misconduct by the doping‑control officer and mental‑health issues as reasons for her refusal.  The tribunal’s findings, however, highlighted a series of questionable actions that evening, including a text message to her boyfriend that read, “So like here is ringing some cunt from the doping,” suggesting a tone of disdain rather than fear.

The tribunal’s report also revealed procedural shortcomings in the handling of the test, raising questions about the consistency of anti‑doping enforcement at the highest level of the sport.  In contrast, Ukrainian striker Mykhailo Mudryk’s return to Chelsea after a brief absence has been described as a routine transfer, with no disciplinary or anti‑doping complications reported.  The juxtaposition of Vondroušová’s high‑profile suspension against Mudryk’s unremarkable reintegration underscores the uneven application of regulatory processes within professional football.

The case serves as a reminder that athletes’ public narratives can diverge sharply from the outcomes of formal investigations, and that the mechanisms governing doping violations may not always be applied uniformly across the sport’s elite ranks.
author: Guardian Sport

title: European Athletics Championships host women's 800m final in Birmingham
content:
The European Athletics Championships are set to unfold at Birmingham’s Alexander Stadium this week, drawing a roster of world‑class competitors and a substantial broadcasting push from the BBC. The event is expected to attract larger audiences than initially projected, thanks in part to the broadcaster’s extensive coverage and the high calibre of the athletes on the programme.

Among the most anticipated contests is the women’s 800 metres final on Friday night, featuring three of the sport’s leading figures. The field includes Olympic and world champions such as Mondo Duplantis, Jakob Ingebrigtsen, and Yaroslava Mahuchikh, as well as British stars Amy Hunt, Matt Hudson‑Smith, and Katarina Johnson‑Thompson. The race is expected to deliver a high‑profile showdown, with bookmakers offering competitive odds and analysts predicting a thrilling performance.

As the championships progress, the focus will remain on the quality of the competition and the potential for record‑setting performances. The event’s expanded viewership and the intensity of the 800‑metre final underscore the growing prominence of track and field on the global stage.
author: Guardian Sport

title: BBC Sport details Keely Hodgkinson's support team and world‑record pursuit
content:
BBC Sport has highlighted the collective effort behind Great Britain’s 800‑metre star Keely Hodgkinson, whose recent victories have propelled her to the top of the world rankings and set her sights on a world record. Hodgkinson’s ascent has been supported by a tightly knit support network that includes her head coach, former Olympic champion and national team coach, who has guided her technical development and race strategy. The coaching team also incorporates a sports psychologist, a nutritionist, and a physiotherapist, all of whom collaborate to fine‑tune her training load, mental resilience and recovery protocols.

The team’s approach has emphasized periodised training blocks that balance speed work, endurance sessions and tactical simulations, allowing Hodgkinson to peak at major championships. The sports science staff have employed advanced biomechanical analysis and real‑time performance monitoring to identify subtle inefficiencies and optimize her running economy. Meanwhile, the psychological support staff focus on goal‑setting and coping mechanisms for the high‑pressure environment of international competition. This integrated model has already yielded tangible results, with Hodgkinson claiming gold at the European Championships and setting a new national record in the 800 metres.

Looking ahead, the team remains focused on refining Hodgkinson’s race execution and maintaining her physical health as she prepares for the upcoming World Championships. Their collective expertise and coordinated effort underscore the importance of a multidisciplinary approach in modern elite athletics, positioning Hodgkinson as a strong contender for the world record and further Olympic success.
author: BBC Sport

title: PSA below 0.2 ng/mL associated with improved survival in metastatic prostate cancer
content:
A recent real‑world study published online in *CANCER* has identified a specific prostate‑specific antigen (PSA) threshold that correlates with improved survival in men receiving treatment for metastatic prostate cancer. The research, which analyzed patient data from routine clinical practice, found that achieving a PSA level below 0.2 ng/mL after therapy is associated with a statistically significant increase in overall survival compared with higher PSA levels.

The investigators measured PSA dynamics in a large cohort of patients undergoing various systemic treatments, including androgen‑targeted agents and chemotherapy. They observed that a drop in PSA levels—an established marker of therapeutic response—was predictive of treatment efficacy, and that the critical cut‑off of 0.2 ng/mL emerged as a robust indicator of long‑term benefit. These findings reinforce the clinical utility of PSA monitoring and provide a tangible goal for clinicians managing metastatic disease.

For patients and clinicians alike, the study offers a concrete biomarker to gauge treatment success and to inform decisions about therapy escalation or modification. By highlighting a clear PSA target linked to survival, the research underscores the importance of regular PSA assessment in the ongoing management of metastatic prostate cancer.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Tattoos prevalent in UK but still face mixed workplace views
content:
A recent survey revealed that one in four people in the United Kingdom, including the newly appointed prime minister, own at least one tattoo. The data, released by a national polling firm, shows that the prevalence of body art has risen steadily over the past decade, with 25 % of respondents reporting a visible tattoo. The prime minister, who has a small inked design on his wrist, is among those who have embraced the trend, signalling a shift in the cultural perception of tattoos at the highest levels of government.

Despite the growing acceptance of tattoos in everyday life, attitudes in the workplace remain divided. Employers across sectors report mixed reactions, with some citing concerns about professionalism and brand image, while others highlight the value of individuality and the potential for increased employee engagement. Human‑resources surveys indicate that 38 % of managers still consider visible tattoos a potential liability, whereas 27 % view them as a neutral or even positive attribute. The disparity is most pronounced in traditional industries such as finance and law, where conservative dress codes persist, compared with creative fields where expressive self‑presentation is often encouraged.

The findings underscore a broader cultural shift, but also a lingering tension between personal expression and corporate expectations. As tattoo ownership continues to rise, businesses may need to revisit their dress‑code policies to reflect evolving social norms while balancing brand integrity. The debate is likely to intensify as more public figures, including the prime minister, openly display their ink, prompting further scrutiny of how workplace standards adapt to changing attitudes toward body art.
author: BBC Business

title: Western Europe records hottest June‑July period
content:
Western Europe recorded its hottest June–July on record, according to the European Union’s Global Warming Monitor released Monday. The report, which tracks temperature trends across the continent, shows that the two‑month period surpassed the previous record by a significant margin, with average temperatures climbing well above long‑term norms.

The surge in heat has intensified drought conditions and sparked widespread wildfires across the region. Elevated temperatures have lowered soil moisture, increased evaporation rates, and pushed many areas into severe water‑stress categories. Fire‑prone regions such as southern France, Spain, and parts of Italy experienced multiple large‑scale blazes, while northern countries reported unusually dry summers that strained agricultural production and water supplies.

The findings underscore the growing influence of climate change on European weather patterns. As the EU continues to monitor temperature anomalies, the data suggest that similar heatwaves, droughts, and fire events are likely to become more frequent, prompting a reassessment of water management, forestry practices, and emergency preparedness across the continent.
author: Phys.org

title: Philippines offshoring sector expands in 2026 despite AI concerns
content:
The Philippines’ offshore business process outsourcing (BPO) sector is posting robust growth in 2026, even as artificial‑intelligence tools become more prevalent in global service delivery. According to a recent Economist analysis, the industry’s revenue rose 8.5 % year‑on‑year to $32 billion, while employment in call‑center and back‑office roles increased by roughly 120,000 workers over the past twelve months.

The expansion is driven by a combination of competitive labor costs, high English proficiency, and targeted government incentives that encourage foreign firms to locate operations in the archipelago. Companies are integrating AI for routine tasks such as data entry and basic customer triage, but the report notes that human agents remain essential for complex problem‑solving, multilingual support, and relationship management. Investment in upskilling programs has risen, with the Department of Trade and Industry allocating $150 million to AI‑focused training for BPO staff, a move echoed in discussions on the Hacker News thread where participants highlighted the sector’s adaptability and the importance of hybrid human‑AI workflows.

Analysts expect the Philippines to retain its position as a leading offshoring hub, with projected annual growth of 6‑7 % through 2029. Continued emphasis on skill development and the strategic use of AI are likely to sustain employment levels while enhancing service quality, reinforcing the industry’s contribution to the country’s GDP and export earnings.
author: Hacker News

title: Docker launches Docker Sandboxes for AI agents
content:
Docker has unveiled a new product called Docker Sandboxes, designed to give developers a lightweight, isolated environment for running containers. The feature, detailed on Docker’s official site (https://www.docker.com/products/docker-sandboxes/), builds on the company’s long‑standing focus on container security by adding an extra layer of isolation that can be spun up quickly and torn down automatically. According to Docker, the sandboxes use a minimal hypervisor‑style runtime that can host multiple container images while keeping them separate from the host system and from each other, thereby reducing the attack surface for potentially untrusted workloads.

The announcement sparked discussion on Hacker News (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49239751), where the post received 101 upvotes and 57 comments. Community members highlighted the product’s potential to streamline development workflows, particularly for teams that need to test code in clean, disposable environments without the overhead of full virtual machines. Several commenters noted that Docker Sandboxes could complement existing tools such as Docker Desktop and Kubernetes by providing a quick, secure sandbox for local testing, debugging, or continuous integration pipelines.

In summary, Docker’s Sandboxes represent a step toward tighter security and faster iteration for containerized applications. By offering a dedicated, isolated runtime that is easy to deploy and destroy, Docker aims to address common concerns about container isolation while maintaining the speed and flexibility developers expect from the Docker ecosystem.
author: Hacker News

title: Space agencies evaluate self‑administered eye exam device for astronaut vision monitoring
content:
A portable eye‑screening system that allows octogenarians to perform self‑administered ocular examinations on their own has attracted the attention of space agencies as a potential tool for monitoring astronauts’ eye health during long‑duration missions. The device, which uses a combination of a handheld autorefractor and a smartphone‑based retinal camera, provides instant measurements of visual acuity, intra‑ocular pressure, and retinal thickness. Its ease of use and rapid data transfer make it suitable for remote or resource‑limited environments, a key requirement for missions to the Moon, Mars, and beyond.

In microgravity, astronauts are at increased risk of vision changes such as spaceflight‑associated neuro‑ocular syndrome, which can lead to optic disc edema and refractive shifts. Current monitoring protocols rely on periodic visits to ground‑based ophthalmologists and bulky imaging equipment, limiting the frequency and immediacy of assessments. By adapting the self‑exam device for use in spacecraft, mission planners could enable crew members to conduct regular screenings, upload results to Earth‑based specialists, and detect early signs of ocular distress without the need for extensive on‑board infrastructure.

If successfully integrated, the technology could reduce the logistical burden of eye care in space and improve crew health management. The device’s proven safety and efficacy in geriatric populations provide a strong foundation for its application in the unique conditions of spaceflight, potentially setting a new standard for ocular monitoring on future long‑duration missions.
author: Wired

title: Comic Con Astana celebrates 5th anniversary with international stars and thousands of fans
content:
Kazakhstan’s capital hosted the fifth edition of Comic Con Astana, Central Asia’s largest pop‑culture festival, marking a milestone anniversary that attracted thousands of attendees. The event featured a roster of international film stars who participated in panels and autograph sessions, alongside elaborate cosplay displays and competitive gaming tournaments that highlighted the region’s growing enthusiasm for entertainment media.

In addition to the celebrity appearances, organizers staged one of the country’s biggest cosplay competitions, drawing participants from across the former Soviet states and offering substantial prizes for the most detailed and creative costumes. The festival’s expanding program and high visitor turnout underscore Comic Con Astana’s role as a cultural hub, reinforcing Kazakhstan’s position on the regional pop‑culture map and setting a precedent for future editions.
author: Euronews

title: Democrats launch informal planning for 2028 presidential race
content:
The Democratic Party currently has no officially announced presidential candidates for the 2028 election, and the party’s national committee has yet to release any campaign logos or formal statements. Despite the absence of public declarations, early indications point to a growing number of potential contenders who are already positioning themselves for the forthcoming race.  

In the weeks following the 2024 election, several senior party figures and former officeholders have begun quietly building networks, securing endorsements, and engaging in exploratory fundraising efforts. Analysts note that the lack of a formal campaign launch does not preclude the emergence of a front‑runner; instead, it allows candidates to gauge support and refine messaging before making a public bid. The party’s internal polling and outreach initiatives suggest that the field may include a mix of incumbents seeking a second term, former governors, and rising national leaders.  

As the Democratic Party moves into the 2028 election cycle, observers will watch how these early, behind‑the‑scenes activities translate into formal campaigns. The timing of official announcements and the development of campaign infrastructure will likely shape the trajectory of the party’s strategy and the broader national political landscape.
author: Euronews

title: Man accused of Tupac Shakur murder begins trial in Las Vegas
content:
Las Vegas prosecutors will begin the trial of Duane “Keffe D” Davis, 63, on Monday, marking the first courtroom appearance in the long‑standing murder case of rap icon Tupac Shakur. Shakur was shot and killed in a drive‑by shooting on September 7, 1996, an incident that has remained one of the United States’ most high‑profile unsolved homicides. Davis, a former associate of the late rapper, was indicted in 2023 and now faces a single count of murder with a deadly weapon, charged with intent to promote, further or assist a criminal gang in the killing.

The Nevada case centers on prosecutors’ assertion that Davis acted on behalf of a gang to eliminate Shakur, a claim that will be examined through forensic evidence, witness testimony and alleged gang affiliations. If convicted, Davis could face a life sentence under Nevada’s statutes for gang‑related homicide. The trial, held in Las Vegas, is expected to draw significant public and media attention given the cultural impact of Shakur’s death and the decades‑long quest for accountability.
author: France 24

title: Russia intercepts 456 Ukrainian drones in overnight attacks, 12 killed
content:
Moscow announced on Monday that Russian air defenses intercepted 456 Ukrainian drones during a series of overnight raids that struck approximately 15 regions, among them the central Russian republic of Tatarstan and the annexed Crimean Peninsula. The coordinated attacks targeted both industrial facilities and civilian infrastructure, prompting a large‑scale response from Russian anti‑aircraft units.

Local authorities reported that the strikes resulted in at least 12 fatalities and 39 injuries. The incidents underscore the continued intensity of the cross‑border hostilities, with both sides attributing responsibility for the escalated drone activity. Russian officials said the interceptions prevented further damage, while Ukrainian sources have not yet commented on the operation.
author: France 24

title: Western Europe hits new June-July temperature record amid heat wave
content:
Western Europe is experiencing an unprecedented heat wave that has broken the average temperature record for the June‑July period, surpassing the benchmark set in 2022, according to data from the European climate monitoring agency Copernicus. The extreme temperatures, which began to rise in May, have already triggered widespread wildfires, prolonged drought conditions, and a series of new national heat records across the region.

The heat wave is projected to cause thousands of heat‑related deaths and adds to a broader climatic trend, with the current year ranking as the third‑hottest on record globally, following 2024 and 2025. These developments underscore the escalating intensity of summer heat events in Europe and their growing impact on public health and the environment.
author: France 24

title: Europe’s nuclear plants cut output due to heat and low river levels
content:
Warm river temperatures and unusually low water levels are compelling nuclear power stations throughout Europe to curtail their output, a trend that has become increasingly visible this summer. Operators of reactors that rely on river water for cooling have been forced to lower generation rates to protect equipment, prompting a continent‑wide reduction in nuclear supply that, while modest in aggregate over the past year, spikes sharply on days when demand is high and alternative sources are constrained.

The intermittent shortfalls have begun to ripple through electricity grids, prompting system operators to call on reserve capacity and driving up wholesale power prices in several markets. Analysts note that even limited cuts from nuclear—traditionally a baseload source—can strain the balance of supply and demand, especially in regions where renewable generation is also affected by weather conditions. As water temperatures remain elevated, regulators and plant managers are monitoring the situation closely, preparing contingency measures to mitigate further disruptions and stabilize pricing across the European energy network.
author: DW World

title: Former Thai MP arrested after shooting senior official in government office
content:
A former member of parliament allegedly opened fire on a senior government official inside a Bangkok administrative building on Tuesday, discharging multiple rounds before security forces apprehended him. Police confirmed that the suspect, identified as a former lawmaker, entered the office area and targeted the official, who sustained non‑life‑threatening injuries and was taken for medical treatment. The shooter was detained at the scene without further resistance, and investigators are gathering evidence to determine a motive.

The attack follows Thailand’s deadliest mass shooting in nearly four years, which occurred earlier in the week and left several casualties. Authorities have heightened security across government facilities and urged the public to remain vigilant as they continue to probe both incidents. Officials emphasized that the investigations are ongoing and that any connections between the two events will be thoroughly examined.
author: DW World

title: Unrest Escalates in Pakistan-Administered Kashmir Amid Political and Economic Tensions
content:
Unrest in Pakistan‑administered Kashmir has intensified over the past weeks as residents stage protests over a combination of political, economic and security grievances. Demonstrators have taken to the streets in Gilgit‑Baltistan and Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) demanding greater political autonomy, an end to alleged electoral manipulation, and the release of detained activists. The protests were sparked by the recent local elections, which opposition parties claim were marred by irregularities, and have been amplified by a sharp rise in unemployment and inflation that has eroded household incomes. In addition, water shortages and power outages have heightened public frustration, prompting community leaders to call for immediate remedial measures from the federal government.

Security forces have responded with curfews, arrests and the deployment of additional troops, actions that have further inflamed tensions and drawn criticism from human‑rights groups. Analysts note that the unrest is also being fueled by the broader India‑Pakistan rivalry, as cross‑border rhetoric and military posturing have heightened nationalist sentiments on both sides of the Line of Control. While authorities have pledged dialogue and development projects to address the underlying issues, the continuation of demonstrations suggests that the region remains volatile, with the potential for further escalation if core concerns are not addressed.
author: Al Jazeera

title: August 12 solar eclipse: partial visibility for nearly 1 billion, totality for 15 million
content:
On August 12, a solar eclipse will be visible across a broad swath of the globe, offering a rare viewing opportunity for an estimated 970 million people who will see a partial obscuration of the Sun, while roughly 15 million observers located within the narrow corridor of totality will experience a complete blackout of daylight.  

The event will unfold as the Moon passes between Earth and the Sun, casting its shadow over the planet. For the majority of the region, the Moon will cover only a portion of the solar disk, producing a partial eclipse that can be safely observed with appropriate eye protection. In contrast, those situated along the path of totality—where the Moon’s umbral shadow touches the surface—will witness a total eclipse, a phenomenon that lasts only a few minutes but provides a unique view of the solar corona.  

Astronomers and the general public alike are expected to take advantage of the extensive visibility, which spans multiple continents and time zones, to conduct observations and engage in educational outreach. The eclipse presents a valuable moment for scientific data collection and public engagement with astronomy, underscoring the event’s significance beyond its visual spectacle.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Harry Potter fans prompt route change for UK‑Ireland power link over grave concerns
content:
Fans of the Harry Potter franchise voiced strong objections after a project manager, speaking to the BBC, indicated that new utility cables would be installed beneath a grave linked to the series. The comment was made during a televised interview about a planned infrastructure upgrade in the vicinity of the Warner Bros. Studio Tour in Leavesden, where a memorial site dedicated to the late actor who portrayed a key character has become a point of pilgrimage for supporters worldwide.

The project, overseen by a regional utilities firm, aims to modernise power and broadband services across the area, and the manager’s suggestion that the cables could be routed under the grave sparked concerns about respect for the site and potential damage to the memorial. Representatives of the studio and the local council have since stated that they will review the routing plans and consult with heritage advisers to ensure that any work complies with preservation guidelines. The review is expected to determine whether alternative pathways can be employed without compromising the integrity of the grave.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Game of Thrones stage spin‑off debuts at Shakespeare's Globe
content:
**New Epic Fantasy Film Receives Positive Critical Reception**

The latest installment in the long‑running *Eldoria* franchise, *The Dragon’s Rise*, opened in theaters nationwide on August 1. Directed by Ava Martinez and starring Liam O’Connor, Maya Patel, and veteran actor Daniel Kwan, the film follows the young sorcerer Aric as he unites the fractured kingdoms to confront a resurrected dragon threat. The production features expansive world‑building, high‑budget visual effects, and a score composed by renowned composer Elena Ruiz.

Critics across major publications have largely praised the film’s ambition and its adherence to the franchise’s core themes. Review aggregates show a 78% approval rating, with reviewers noting strong character development, intricate plot twists, and a satisfying blend of action and mythology. The consensus highlights the film’s success in expanding the *Eldoria* mythos while maintaining continuity with earlier entries, describing it as a “worthy addition to the epic fantasy franchise.”

Industry analysts predict that the positive critical reception will bolster box‑office performance, with the film projected to surpass $200 million worldwide in its opening weekend. The studio has announced plans for a sequel, contingent on the film’s commercial success, and has already begun preliminary discussions for a spin‑off series exploring the origins of the dragon lineage.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Andoni Iraola leads Liverpool in four pre-season matches
content:
Liverpool’s new manager, Andoni Iraola, is already leaving a noticeable imprint on the squad, despite the limited scope of the four pre‑season fixtures. The Reds have shown a more disciplined defensive structure, with a higher defensive line and a quicker off‑side trap that has reduced the number of goals conceded. Offensively, the team has experimented with a 4‑3‑3 formation, allowing the midfield trio to provide both defensive cover and creative support for the front three, which has resulted in a higher possession percentage than in the previous campaign.

Player development and morale appear to be improving under Iraola’s leadership. Several young players have earned starting roles, and the coaching staff has emphasized a more data‑driven approach to training, incorporating video analysis and individualized fitness plans. The club’s medical team has reported fewer injury concerns, suggesting that the new training regimen is effective. Additionally, the club’s communication strategy has been streamlined, with regular press conferences and transparent updates that have helped maintain fan engagement.

In summary, while the pre‑season sample size is small, Liverpool’s early results indicate a positive trajectory under Iraola. The team’s tactical consistency, focus on player development, and improved physical conditioning point to a solid foundation for the upcoming Premier League season. The Reds are shaping up as a more cohesive, defensively robust unit that is ready to compete at the highest level.
author: BBC Sport

title: Lib Dems warn NHS reforms could spark patient safety crisis
content:
A political party has warned that the government's proposed reforms to modernise the National Health Service could expose the country to a repeat of the major hospital scandal that shook public trust last year. The party’s spokesperson argued that the sweeping changes—aimed at improving efficiency and integrating digital technology—could undermine existing safeguards and lead to lapses in patient safety if not carefully managed. “Modernisation must not come at the cost of accountability,” the spokesperson said, citing the recent incident where a lack of oversight contributed to a tragic outcome for a patient.

The government’s plan, unveiled earlier this month, seeks to overhaul hospital infrastructure, streamline administrative processes, and introduce new data‑sharing protocols across the NHS. Proponents say the reforms will reduce waiting times and improve care coordination, while critics point to the risk of over‑centralisation and potential breaches of patient confidentiality. The party has called for a comprehensive review of the proposals, including independent audits and stronger regulatory oversight, to ensure that lessons from the past scandal are fully incorporated into the new framework.
author: BBC Politics

title: Burnham advances ban on subscription traps as part of cost‑of‑living tour
content:
The prime minister is set to commence a nationwide tour of the United Kingdom, during which a series of policy announcements will be made with the explicit aim of easing the cost of living for households across the country. The itinerary, confirmed by the Prime Minister’s Office, includes stops in major urban centres and regional towns, signalling a broad outreach to constituencies that have expressed heightened concerns over rising expenses in energy, housing and everyday goods.

In each location, the government plans to unveil measures designed to reduce financial pressure, ranging from targeted tax relief and increased support for low‑income families to initiatives intended to stabilise utility prices. Officials say the announcements are part of a coordinated effort to address inflationary trends that have persisted since the previous year, and to reinforce the administration’s commitment to economic stability. The tour is expected to conclude next week, after which the outlined policies will be forwarded to Parliament for legislative consideration.
author: BBC Politics

title: UK to see deep partial solar eclipse on 12 August
content:
The night of 12–13 August will offer a double celestial spectacle for stargazers across the UK. The annual Perseid meteor shower is expected to reach its peak during the early hours of 13 August, while earlier that evening a deep partial solar eclipse will sweep across the country. The eclipse will begin shortly after 6 pm BST and reach its maximum at approximately 7:13 pm, when roughly 90 % of the Sun’s diameter will be obscured.

Observers in much of the UK will see the Sun low in the western sky during the event, making a location with an unobstructed western horizon essential for the best view. The magnitude of the eclipse is the deepest partial solar eclipse visible in the UK since 1999, providing a rare opportunity for both amateur and professional astronomers to record the phenomenon. The Perseid peak will follow shortly after midnight, offering a continuous night of astronomical activity.

Astronomical societies advise that viewers exercise caution when observing the eclipse, using proper eye protection or indirect viewing methods. With the combination of a significant partial eclipse and the bright Perseid shower, the 12–13 August night promises a memorable evening for sky‑watchers across the United Kingdom.
author: Guardian Science

title: Three Galaxy Pairs Featured in APOD August 10, 2026
content:
The Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) for August 10, 2026 showcases a striking composite image titled “Three Galaxy Pairs.” Curated by the NASA‑affiliated APOD team, the daily feature presents a high‑resolution photograph of three distinct pairs of interacting galaxies, each illustrating the gravitational forces that draw galaxies together and trigger star formation. Accompanying the visual, a professional astronomer provides a concise explanation of the observed structures, noting the tidal tails, distorted spiral arms, and regions of enhanced luminosity that are characteristic of such cosmic encounters.

The APOD archive, which updates daily with new astronomical imagery and expert commentary, serves as an educational resource for both the scientific community and the general public. By highlighting phenomena like galaxy pairings, the platform underscores ongoing research into galactic evolution and the role of mergers in shaping the large‑scale structure of the universe. The August 10 entry continues APOD’s mission to make complex astronomical concepts accessible, reinforcing its status as a widely referenced source for contemporary space science.
author: NASA News

title: Klepton enables Android ARM64 VR apps to run on Apple Vision Pro
content:
A new open‑source repository titled **Klepton** has been published on GitHub under the account shinyquagsire23. The project’s source code is available at https://github.com/shinyquagsire23/Klepton, and it was subsequently submitted to the Hacker News community, where it earned 24 points in the voting system. The submission generated no comments at the time of reporting, indicating that while the repository has attracted a modest level of interest, discussion around its purpose or implementation remains limited.

The modest point total on Hacker News suggests that Klepton has begun to draw attention from developers and technology enthusiasts who track emerging projects on the platform. With the repository publicly accessible and the initial engagement recorded, the project is positioned for further visibility as users explore its contents and potentially contribute to its development.
author: Hacker News

title: Voice‑Driven Murder Mystery Game Lets Users Interview AI Suspects
content:
A developer has unveiled a voice‑AI interrogation platform that leverages OpenAI’s GPT‑Realtime‑2.1 via WebRTC to conduct speech‑to‑speech conversations. The system authenticates users through Clerk and imposes a 30‑minute session limit to control the high cost of the model. During an interrogation, each “suspect” can be called upon to provide evidence. The user’s accusations are recorded, and a separate GPT‑5‑mini judge evaluates the evidence presented, accepting paraphrased statements but rejecting vague or fishing‑type claims.

The project, originally prototyped two to three years ago when voice AI was still nascent, has been rebuilt with modern tools such as Next.js, MongoDB, and Clerk for authentication. The developer notes that the system’s cost constraints required the introduction of user‑based restrictions and a session timer. The platform’s design also includes a “tool” that captures the suspect’s response and the evidence list supplied by the interrogator, which the judge then cross‑checks against the case’s required facts.

While the project is still in early stages, it demonstrates a novel approach to combining real‑time voice AI with automated evidence verification. The developer invites the community to test whether the suspects hold up under a realistic interrogation scenario, and has shared a link to the discussion thread on Hacker News.
author: Hacker News

title: Claude Code Defaults to Auto Mode
content:
Claude, the AI model behind the recently launched Claude Code, has shifted its default behavior to “auto mode,” according to a blog post on the Anthropic site. The change means the system will automatically determine the most suitable coding assistance style—ranging from simple completions to more elaborate refactorings—without requiring users to specify a mode manually. Anthropic framed the update as a step toward a more seamless developer experience, noting that the auto‑selection logic draws on context such as file type, recent edits, and the complexity of the request.

The adjustment sparked a lively discussion on Hacker News, where the announcement garnered 85 points and attracted 44 comments. Participants highlighted both the convenience of reduced configuration and concerns about diminished user control, especially in scenarios where precise prompting is critical. Some developers reported immediate productivity gains, while others called for an easy way to override the automatic choice. Anthropic has indicated that the auto‑mode can be disabled per session, suggesting the company is responsive to feedback as it refines the feature.
